pr.title: feat(accounts): resolve or provision OIDC users
pr.author: gilmishal
pr.head: 4142977c6

lead.heading: What the change accomplishes
lead.text: PR #2224 lets a user's first sign-in create their FloxHub account automatically. It adds an internal accounts endpoint that web-bff calls at login with the user's identity and profile claims. The endpoint returns the existing user or creates one, so there is no separate registration step. Only callers holding an internal API key can use it, and it is available on every deployment, SaaS included.

lead.heading: What's new: accounts created from the login itself
lead.text: On a first login, the service derives the new account from the identity provider's data. The user id is computed from the provider's issuer and subject, so the same identity always gets the same id. The handle comes from the preferred username, or from the name when that is missing, using the rules web-bff already applies. The service then grants the user ownership in FGA. If two first logins race, both get the winning request's account; if the handle is taken, the login fails with 409. Every later login re-applies the FGA grants, so a grant lost to an FGA outage is repaired the next time the user signs in.

verdict: The code does what the description says on every path I could run, including two the PR's own tests don't reach: two simultaneous first logins, and FGA failing after the account is saved. The defects are at the edges and in the written material: a malformed API key crashes the endpoint instead of being rejected, the endpoint refuses a lowercase 'bearer' that the rest of the service accepts, the published API description lists the wrong response codes, and three written statements are false.
limit_line: Nothing here used a real FGA store, two truly simultaneous database transactions (the race probe fakes a missed lookup instead), the production web server's header handling (the malformed-key probe ran through the test client), or the deployed routing on either environment.
risk_pointer: Proposed risk: low to medium. The change only adds an internal endpoint behind an API key and alters nothing that exists, but the ids and handles it creates are stored permanently, so a mistake in how they are derived would need a data fix rather than a redeploy. A test now pins how ids are computed.

sections.title: Correctness
sections.blurb: What I could verify by running or reading. `Did not hold` is what the reader acts on; `Held` is the evidence behind the verdict.

items.summary: An API key containing a non-ASCII character crashes the endpoint with a 500 instead of a 401
items.detail: Anyone can send a key containing a character such as 'é' and get a server error instead of 'unauthorized'. No credentials are needed to trigger it.

items.summary: The internal endpoints refuse 'bearer' in lowercase, though the service's other endpoints accept it
items.detail: A request whose authorization header says 'bearer' instead of 'Bearer' is accepted by the public endpoints in the same service and refused by the internal ones. The standard makes the word case-insensitive (RFC 7235 §2.1), and the service's own 401 response invokes that standard. Nothing breaks today, because web-bff, the only caller, sends 'Bearer'.

items.summary: The published API description lists response codes the endpoints never return, and leaves out the one they do
items.detail: Clients reading the API description are told that provisioning can answer 404, which it no longer does, and are not told that it answers 201 when it creates a user. The lookup endpoint is listed as answering 409 and 503, which it can't. Both endpoints share one list of error codes, and the review fix that removed the 404 case (70fec72d1) left it in the list. web-bff accepts any success code, so it handles the 201.

items.summary: The accounts `claude.md` describes a token-verification step that was never merged
items.detail: It says claims reach the service only after an 'OIDC token endpoint gate' has verified them. That gate was PR #2221, closed without merging on 2026-08-17. Tokens are actually verified in web-bff's login callback (#2187), so the statement is wrong from the moment this merges.

items.summary: The README says the internal routes can't be reached through the public accounts route, which is false on SaaS by design
items.detail: On SaaS, the public API gateway forwards every accounts path, internal ones included, and web-bff itself reaches accounts through that public address. The API key is the only protection, which is what ENT-225 intends. On-prem the statement becomes true only once #2187 blocks those paths in the proxy.

items.summary: A code comment says a user's email is refreshed at each login; the code never updates it
items.detail: A second login carrying a new email and avatar leaves both unchanged and only records the login time. The code follows ENT-191 ('nothing reads provider claims after creation'); the comment, and the design doc section it came from, say the opposite. Which one is out of date is B1.

items.evidence: mutation: delete the regrant at user_service.py:108, then just accounts test -k test_users
items.summary: The PR's tests would not notice if grants stopped being reapplied after two simultaneous first logins
items.detail: When two first logins race, the losing request is supposed to reapply the winner's FGA grants. I deleted that step and all 8 of the PR's tests still passed. Only the audit's race probe, `test_p3_race_recovers_existing_user`, which makes the second login miss its lookup so its insert collides, caught the deletion.

items.evidence: ENT-191 'Report back on' vs the PR body
items.summary: The PR description doesn't answer the three questions ENT-191 asked to hear back on
items.detail: The answers, read from the code. Callers can't supply their own handle, because the request has no handle field. Operators see `422 {'detail': 'Invalid handle: <length|format|unavailable>'}`, `409 {'detail': 'Handle is unavailable'}`, or `422 {'detail': 'OIDC identity has no preferred_username or name claim'}`. And it did land behind ENT-225's key check: the PR carries its own check, and #2226 set up the key in terraform first.

items.evidence: CI run 32853773279 on 4142977c6; just accounts test in the audit worktree
items.summary: CI passes on the latest commit, and all 117 tests pass locally
items.detail: CI run 32853773279 on `4142977c6` passed every job, including all the integration tests. The probe file is `src/accounts/tests/test_audit_probes.py` in the audit worktree, untracked; `just accounts test -k test_p` runs it.

items.summary: If FGA fails after the account is saved, the account survives and the next login grants ownership
items.detail: With FGA failing after the save, the user exists without grants. A second login returns 200 and writes both ownership grants, as the PR claims.

items.summary: Two simultaneous first logins end up with the same account, with its grants in place
items.detail: The probe makes the second login miss its lookup so its insert collides. It returns 200 with the first login's user and both grants reapplied.

items.summary: An empty key setting refuses every request, and a list of keys accepts each one
items.detail: With the key setting empty, or only commas and spaces, every request is refused, including one sending an empty key. With `'k1, k2 ,'` both keys work, and `k1` with a trailing space does not. The PR's own tests cover missing and wrong keys but not an empty setting.

items.evidence: node vs python3 over 15 inputs; test_p7_normalization
items.summary: Handles come out exactly as web-bff would make them
items.detail: 15 tricky names run through web-bff's version and the new one give identical handles; for example 'Zoë Müller' becomes `zo-m-ller` and 'İstanbul' becomes `i-stanbul`. Reserved names such as `flox-admin`, UUID-shaped names, and names that reduce to nothing are rejected with 422.

items.summary: A handle collision leaves nothing behind
items.detail: After the 409, the database holds only the existing user. No stray identity, user or handle is created, and the losing identity is not linked to anyone.

items.evidence: mutations: delete the regrant in _record_login; change the uuid5 separator
items.summary: The PR's tests would catch a change to the regrant on login or to how user ids are computed
items.detail: Removing the regrant on login, or changing how the id is computed from issuer and subject, each makes one of the PR's tests fail.

items.evidence: ENT-191 Must / Must not vs the diff
items.summary: Every ENT-191 requirement that belongs to accounts is met
items.detail: Must 1, 2, 3 and 5 and Must-not 2 and 3 are met here. Must 4 and Must-not 1 belong to web-bff, in #2187.

items.summary: This PR and web-bff's side, #2187, agree on the endpoint path, request fields, auth header and key setting
items.detail: Both use the same path, the same request fields, an `Authorization: Bearer` header, and the `FLOXHUB_ACCOUNTS_INTERNAL_API_KEYS` setting, which terraform (#2226) and the dev shell already provide.

sections.title: Decisions the PR made that only you can judge
sections.blurb: Each item names a choice the author already encoded, what it turns on, where that is grounded, and what stays if you say nothing. Ordered by what reading the PR will not reveal, durable before local — never by significance.

groups.title: Lead — the ones I'd push back on

items.summary: A comment says a user's email is refreshed at login, but the code sets it once at signup; one of the two is wrong
items.turns_on: Whether ENT-191's 'syncing profile data on later logins is additive and out' means never, in which case the comment should change, or not yet, in which case the comment stays as the goal and the code is behind it for now.
items.grounded: ENT-191 for the behavior; design doc §5.1 and the comment for the end state.
items.default: The comment stays as written, and the code doesn't refresh.

items.summary: The PR provisions a user with one call that picks the handle itself, replacing the design doc's two calls, so callers can no longer choose a handle
items.turns_on: Whether the Auth0 Action (ENT-236), or any screen that lets a user pick a handle, can work without passing one in. If not, the endpoint needs a handle field.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must-not #3 for moving handle derivation into accounts; nothing for dropping the design doc's option to supply a handle (§5.1).

items.summary: User ids are computed from the identity provider's issuer and subject, so the same identity always gets the same id, and a test now locks this in
items.turns_on: Whether anything will ever compute a user's id from their login token without looking it up, and whether renaming a Dex connector, which changes subjects, should change users' ids. The ids are stored permanently, so changing the scheme later means migrating data.
items.grounded: Review thread ('leaves that possibility open'); ENT-224 said 'accounts-minted UUID'; design doc §3.1 argues subjects are unstable on-prem. `test_first_login_derives_handle_id_and_personal_ownership` pins the exact derivation.

items.summary: Users created through this endpoint get computed ids, while users created any other way get random ones
items.turns_on: Whether every user's id must be computable from their first login, or only the ids of users created here. The other ways users get created are the Auth0 Action signup (ENT-236) and imports. If anything ever computes a user's id from their token (B3), users created those ways couldn't be found that way.
items.grounded: `models.py:75` records the split ('other writers retain the random default'); nothing found on whether ENT-236 should compute ids the same way.

items.summary: Every login writes the user's FGA grants again, not only a retry after a failure
items.turns_on: Whether an FGA write on every login costs too much compared with repairing grants only when a retry happens.
items.grounded: ENT-227 said 'repaired by retrying the call or by the reconciler'; the PR's `claude.md` recasts it as 'reasserted when provisioned again'.
items.default: Grants are rewritten on every login.

items.summary: On-prem, the internal key is configured only by #2187, so this PR on its own leaves every on-prem internal call failing with 401
items.turns_on: Only the order in which the stack merges.
items.grounded: #2187's diff sets `FLOXHUB_ACCOUNTS_INTERNAL_API_KEYS` from the on-prem secrets directory.
items.default: Nothing changes; the stack order handles it.

items.summary: An empty issuer and subject are accepted and create a user
items.turns_on: Whether callers will always have verified the token before calling.
items.grounded: Nothing in accounts; the audit probe `test_p10_empty_identity_pair` shows an empty pair gets 201.

items.summary: An empty preferred username counts as missing, so the handle comes from the name instead
items.turns_on: Whether Dex ever sends an empty preferred username instead of leaving it out.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must #2 says 'absent'; the `test_p7_normalization` case `'' / 'Fallback Name'` gives `fallback-name`.

items.summary: Users with non-ASCII names get garbled handles, and a name that can't produce a valid handle blocks login with a 422 and no way to pick another
items.turns_on: Whether failing the login is the right outcome for those directory users.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must #3 and 'You may assume #2'.

items.summary: When saving a new user collides with an existing record, the service assumes the handle was taken and answers 409 'Handle is unavailable'
items.turns_on: Whether the handle is the only thing that can collide. Today it is. If a unique field is added later, such as a unique email, its collisions would be misreported as a taken handle.
items.grounded: The schema in `models.py`: `email` is not unique, and a user id can only collide when the identity was already linked.
items.default: Any collision is reported as a taken handle.

items.summary: A taken handle answers 409, invalid login data answers 422, and any other error is a 500
items.turns_on: What web-bff and operators do with each code, and whether invalid input should answer 400 instead of 422.
items.grounded: ENT-227 for 409; nothing for 422 over 400.

items.summary: Error messages say why a login was rejected but never include the handle or username
items.turns_on: Whether handles may be sent to Sentry, which is unsettled.
items.grounded: Consistent with the contested position in AI-178.
items.default: Handles stay out of error messages.

items.summary: New users are marked as having finished signup and onboarding immediately
items.turns_on: Whether on-prem has an onboarding step these flags should hold users at.
items.grounded: web-bff's on-prem services already report both as finished (`PosixUserService.ts:49`, `AccountsUserService.ts:22`).

items.summary: When there's no preferred username, the user's name becomes both their handle and their display name
items.turns_on: What display name a user who only has a username should get.
items.grounded: Nothing beyond the ticket naming the name as the fallback for the username.
items.default: The name is used for both.

items.summary: The internal endpoints are available on every deployment, including SaaS, where the API key is their only protection
items.turns_on: Whether exposing them on SaaS behind the key is acceptable.
items.grounded: ENT-225's outcome ('reachable from the internet, the key is the only thing in front').

items.summary: The user lookup takes the user id in its address instead of in the shared header ENT-225 requires for the end user
items.turns_on: Whether ENT-225's header rule applies to a lookup made while a session is still being set up.
items.grounded: ENT-225; the PR doesn't address it.
items.default: The id stays in the address.

items.summary: The key setting is a comma-separated list, with spaces ignored, and defaults to empty
items.turns_on: The format of the stored secret in SSM.
items.grounded: ENT-225 Must #1; terraform's `/floxhub/{env}/accounts/internal-api-keys`.

items.summary: The PR forces an early database write between saving the user and saving their identity, and removing it changes nothing
items.turns_on: Nothing today: the database library already saves the user first on its own, and with the extra write removed all the PR's tests and the audit probes still pass.
items.grounded: Mutation run (`just accounts test -k test_users`, then `-k test_p`, with the line removed).

items.summary: The PR links each identity to its user but not each user to their identities, so finding a user's identities takes a query
items.turns_on: Whether something will need to go from a user to their identities. The reconciler snapshot in design doc §5.8, which ENT-231 builds, does exactly that. It can query identities by user id, or add the reverse link (`User.identities`); a reverse link added later without `back_populates` can disagree with the forward one within a session until it is saved and reloaded.
items.grounded: The link was added at review so that the types show every identity has a user (Nick's comment on 8faf18306, fixed in 70fec72d1). Design doc §5.8 for the coming user-to-identities walk.
items.default: One-way stays; a consumer that needs the reverse direction queries identities by user id.

items.summary: The PR has no test for reapplying grants after two simultaneous first logins
items.turns_on: Whether to keep the audit's race probe, or a version with two real transactions, as a permanent test.
